An XCAT Chest With Custom Materials

Scan a digital anatomy whose materials you define, down to a contrast agent built from its elements.

Notebook 01 walked the five-struct API on a calibration phantom. This notebook swaps the phantom for a voxelized XCAT adult-male chest and gives each tissue its own XrayAttenuation.Material, with an iodinated blood pool (a CT angiography bolus) built inline, then compares FBP with Hybrid IR on the same scan.

PhantomXCAT adult-male 50th-percentile chest, one axial slab at full resolution (XCIST phantoms-voxelized, downloaded as a Julia artifact)
MaterialsXA.Materials.ncat_* tissues, plus an iodinated-blood material constructed inline
ScannerGE Revolution Apex Elite (as in notebook 01)
ReconstructionFBP and Hybrid IR at strength 60, both after the water beam-hardening correction

Notebook Setup

As in notebook 01: the shared docs/ environment, then the device. Unitful supplies the u"eV" and u"g/cm^3" units the XA.Material constructor takes.

import BasisSimulator as BS

Choosing the Device

GPUSelect.Storage() returns the array type of the GPU it finds (CuArray, MtlArray, ROCArray, oneArray), or Array on a CPU-only host; moving the phantom mask to it decides where the pipeline runs.

begin
    import GPUSelect
    # the backend array type, directly: MtlArray / CuArray / ROCArray
    AT = GPUSelect.Storage()
    to_gpu(x) = AT(x)
    GPU_BACKEND = (name = string(nameof(AT)),)
end;

Backend detected: CuArray

"""A blank drawing area at `position`: equal scales, no axes, limits `(x0, x1, y0, y1)`."""
function canvas(position, limits; background = COLORS.paper)
    ax = Mke.Axis(position; aspect = Mke.DataAspect(), backgroundcolor = background)
    Mke.hidedecorations!(ax)
    Mke.hidespines!(ax)
    Mke.limits!(ax, limits...)
    return ax
end;
"""The corners of a rectangle centred at `c`, `w` × `h`, its corners rounded by `r`."""
function rounded_rect(c, w, h, r)
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = c[1] - w / 2, c[2] - h / 2, c[1] + w / 2, c[2] + h / 2
    r = min(r, w / 2, h / 2)
    arc(cx, cy, θ0) = [
        Mke.Point2f(cx + r * cos(θ), cy + r * sin(θ))
        for θ in range(θ0, θ0 + π / 2; length = 8)
    ]
    return vcat(
        arc(x1 - r, y0 + r, -π / 2),
        arc(x1 - r, y1 - r, 0.0),
        arc(x0 + r, y1 - r, π / 2),
        arc(x0 + r, y0 + r, π),
    )
end;
"""A straight arrow from `a` to `b`; `head` is the arrowhead's size in pixels."""
function arrow!(
    ax,
    a,
    b;
    color = COLORS.muted,
    linewidth = 2.5,
    head = 15,
    linestyle = :solid,
)
    a, b = Mke.Point2f(a), Mke.Point2f(b)
    Mke.lines!(ax, [a, b]; color, linewidth, linestyle)
    t = b - a
    Mke.scatter!(
        ax,
        [b];
        marker = :utriangle,
        markersize = head,
        rotation = atan(t[2], t[1]) - π / 2,
        color,
        markerspace = :pixel,
    )
    return nothing
end;
"""
A box in a flow chart: centred at `c`, `w` × `h`, a bold `title` and an optional smaller
`subtitle`. `accent` colours its outline (and a strip down its left edge).
"""
function node!(
    ax,
    c,
    title;
    subtitle = "",
    w = 3.0,
    h = 1.0,
    accent = COLORS.violet,
    fill = COLORS.card,
    textcolor = COLORS.ink,
    subcolor = COLORS.muted,
    titlesize = 19,
    subtitlesize = 15,
    code = false,
)
    Mke.poly!(
        ax,
        rounded_rect(c, w, h, 0.14);
        color = fill,
        strokecolor = accent,
        strokewidth = 2,
    )
    strip = rounded_rect((c[1] - w / 2 + 0.06, c[2]), 0.12, h - 0.1, 0.05)
    Mke.poly!(ax, strip; color = accent)
    font = code ? "DejaVu Sans Mono Bold" : :bold
    dy = isempty(subtitle) ? 0.0 : 0.17 * h
    Mke.text!(
        ax,
        c[1] + 0.05,
        c[2] + dy;
        text = title,
        align = (:center, :center),
        fontsize = titlesize,
        font,
        color = textcolor,
    )
    isempty(subtitle) ||
        Mke.text!(
            ax,
            c[1] + 0.05,
            c[2] - 0.22 * h;
            text = subtitle,
            align = (:center, :center),
            fontsize = subtitlesize,
            color = subcolor,
        )
    return nothing
end;
"""
A flow chart: `nodes` maps a key to `(x, y, title, subtitle, accent)` (subtitle and accent
optional), `edges` lists `from => to` pairs, drawn as arrows between the boxes' edges, and
`labels` (optional) puts a note on an edge. Returns the canvas.
"""
function flow_chart!(position, nodes, edges; limits, w = 3.0, h = 1.0, labels = Dict())
    ax = canvas(position, limits)
    box(key) = nodes[key]
    function port(from, to)
        a, b = box(from), box(to)
        if abs(b[2] - a[2]) < 1.0e-6
            # side by side
            s = sign(b[1] - a[1])
            return (a[1] + s * w / 2, a[2]), (b[1] - s * w / 2, b[2])
        elseif abs(b[1] - a[1]) < 1.0e-6
            # one above the other
            s = sign(b[2] - a[2])
            return (a[1], a[2] + s * h / 2), (b[1], b[2] - s * h / 2)
        else
            # leave sideways, arrive on the facing side
            s = sign(b[1] - a[1])
            return (a[1] + s * w / 2, a[2]), (b[1] - s * w / 2, b[2])
        end
    end
    for (from, to) in edges
        p, q = port(from, to)
        if abs(p[1] - q[1]) < 1.0e-6 || abs(p[2] - q[2]) < 1.0e-6
            # straight across or straight down
            arrow!(ax, p, q)
        else
            # a right-angled connector: across to the gap's middle, along it, then in
            mx = (p[1] + q[1]) / 2
            Mke.lines!(
                ax,
                Mke.Point2f[p, (mx, p[2]), (mx, q[2])];
                color = COLORS.muted,
                linewidth = 2.5,
            )
            arrow!(ax, (mx, q[2]), q)
        end
        haskey(labels, from => to) &&
            Mke.text!(
                ax,
                (p[1] + q[1]) / 2,
                q[2] + 0.12;
                text = labels[from => to],
                align = (:center, :bottom),
                fontsize = 15,
                color = COLORS.muted,
            )
    end
    for (_, n) in nodes
        node!(
            ax,
            (n[1], n[2]),
            n[3];
            subtitle = length(n) >= 4 ? n[4] : "",
            accent = length(n) >= 5 ? n[5] : COLORS.violet,
            w,
            h,
        )
    end
    return ax
end;
"""
A CT gantry seen along z, centred at the origin: the source(s) at radius `sid` (one per entry
of `angles`, degrees), the fan, the detector arc at `sdd` from each source, and a round object
of radius `r_object`. Draws on `ax` in the colours of `dark` (the locator band) or paper.
"""
function gantry!(
    ax;
    sid = 5.4,
    sdd = 9.5,
    angles = (90.0,),
    fan_deg = 50.0,
    r_object = 2.0,
    detector_colors = (COLORS.cyan,),
    labels = ("Tube",),
    dark = true,
    object = true,
)
    ink = dark ? COLORS.night_ink : COLORS.ink
    ring = dark ? COLORS.night_card : COLORS.card
    Mke.poly!(ax, Mke.Circle(Mke.Point2f(0, 0), sid + 0.9); color = ring)
    Mke.poly!(
        ax,
        Mke.Circle(Mke.Point2f(0, 0), sid - 1.6);
        color = dark ? COLORS.night : COLORS.paper,
    )
    for (k, θ) in enumerate(angles)
        θ = deg2rad(θ)
        s = Mke.Point2f(sid * cos(θ), sid * sin(θ))
        half = deg2rad(fan_deg / 2)
        # the fan, from the focal spot to the detector arc (a circle about the source)
        edge = Mke.Point2f[
            s + sdd * Mke.Point2f(cos(θ + π + φ), sin(θ + π + φ))
            for φ in range(-half, half; length = 40)
        ]
        Mke.poly!(
            ax,
            Mke.Point2f.(vcat([s], edge));
            color = (COLORS.beam, 0.22),
            strokewidth = 0,
        )
        Mke.lines!(ax, edge; color = detector_colors[mod1(k, end)], linewidth = 9)
        Mke.scatter!(ax, [s]; marker = :rect, markersize = 26, color = ink)
        Mke.scatter!(ax, [s]; marker = :circle, markersize = 9, color = COLORS.beam)
        Mke.text!(
            ax,
            s * 1.18;
            text = labels[mod1(k, end)],
            align = (:center, :center),
            fontsize = 17,
            font = :bold,
            color = ink,
        )
    end
    object &&
        Mke.poly!(
            ax,
            Mke.Circle(Mke.Point2f(0, 0), r_object);
            color = (COLORS.blue, 0.55),
            strokecolor = ink,
            strokewidth = 1.5,
        )
    return ax
end;
"""
The dark locator band that opens a notebook: `n` panels side by side, each a canvas with
`limits`, its `titles[i]` and `subtitles[i]` underneath. Returns the figure and the canvases;
draw into them, then show the figure.
"""
function locator_band(titles, subtitles; limits, size = (1500, 560))
    fig = Mke.Figure(;
        size,
        backgroundcolor = COLORS.night,
        figure_padding = (10, 10, 18, 10),
    )
    axes = [
        canvas(fig[1, i], limits[i]; background = COLORS.night)
        for i in eachindex(titles)
    ]
    for i in eachindex(titles)
        Mke.Label(
            fig[2, i],
            titles[i];
            fontsize = 25,
            font = :bold,
            color = COLORS.night_ink,
            tellwidth = false,
        )
        Mke.Label(
            fig[3, i],
            subtitles[i];
            fontsize = 17,
            color = COLORS.night_muted,
            tellwidth = false,
        )
    end
    Mke.rowgap!(fig.layout, 1, 8)
    Mke.rowgap!(fig.layout, 2, 2)
    return fig, axes
end;
blend

c mixed toward base (the paper): t = 1 is c itself, t = 0 is base.

"""`c` mixed toward `base` (the paper): `t = 1` is `c` itself, `t = 0` is `base`."""
function blend(c, t; base = COLORS.paper)
    return Mke.RGBf(
        t * c.r + (1 - t) * base.r,
        t * c.g + (1 - t) * base.g,
        t * c.b + (1 - t) * base.b,
    )
end

TISSUES = Dict(
    "ncat_lung" => (blend(COLORS.cyan, 0.18), "Lung"),
    "ncat_adipose" => (blend(COLORS.beam, 0.45), "Fat"),
    "ncat_muscle" => (blend(COLORS.purple, 0.38), "Muscle"),
    "ncat_heart" => (COLORS.purple, "Myocardium"),
    "ncat_blood" => (COLORS.red, "Blood + 5 mg/mL Iodine"),
    "ncat_dry_spine" => (COLORS.ink, "Spine"),
    "ncat_dry_rib" => (COLORS.muted, "Rib"),
    "ncat_cartilage" => (blend(COLORS.cyan, 0.6), "Cartilage"),
    "ncat_water" => (COLORS.blue, "Water"),
)
draw_tissues!

An XCAT slice of labels drawn on ax in its tissue colours (TISSUES), dx cm per voxel, centred (air left clear; a tissue not in TISSUES is drawn grey).

"""
An XCAT slice of `labels` drawn on `ax` in its tissue colours (`TISSUES`), `dx` cm per voxel,
centred (air left clear; a tissue not in `TISSUES` is drawn grey).
"""
function draw_tissues!(ax, labels, label_names, dx)
    n1, n2 = size(labels)
    colour(l) = haskey(label_names, l) ?
        Mke.RGBAf(get(TISSUES, label_names[l], (COLORS.rule, ""))[1]) :
        Mke.RGBAf(0, 0, 0, 0)
    lut = Dict(l => colour(l) for l in unique(labels))
    Mke.image!(
        ax,
        (-n1 / 2 * dx, n1 / 2 * dx),
        (-n2 / 2 * dx, n2 / 2 * dx),
        [lut[l] for l in labels];
        interpolate = false,
    )
    return ax
end

1. Download the XCAT Phantom

No local files, no manual setup. BS.load_xcat_male_chest() fetches the voxelized XCAT adult-male 50th-percentile chest phantom from the open xcist/phantoms-voxelized repository (BSD-3-Clause) into Julia's content-addressed artifact store: it downloads once, verifies the file's SHA-256 against the value pinned in the package, logs the Segars XCAT + XCIST citation, and reuses the cached copy on every later call.

Using the XCAT loaders

Four phantoms ship: :female_slab, :female_chest, :male_slab, :male_chest (see BS.xcat_phantoms()). Each load_xcat_<name>() returns the labeled pieces: mask, a materials dict (label => XA.Material), label_names and voxel_size_cm, which you turn into a Phantom in one line (section 3). Useful keywords:

  • downsample = n: a label-preserving majority-vote shrink (physical extent preserved). This notebook uses the slab at its full 0.25 mm, so it passes no downsample; reach for it on the full :male_chest volume. It is lossy (a 6× round trip agrees with full resolution on about 96 % of voxels), so treat it as a speed knob, not a lossless representation.

  • materials = Dict("ncat_blood" => …): override the tissue → material map by XCIST name before assembly (section 2).

  • path = …: skip the download and read an already-extracted copy from disk.

  • quiet = true: silence the citation and progress logging.

2. Custom Materials via XrayAttenuation

The loader assigns every label a sensible default tissue, but the point of a digital phantom is that you control the material physics. Each label maps to an XA.Material that gives the simulator its energy-dependent μ(E). There are two ways to get one: prebuilt, XA.Materials.ncat_blood, XA.Materials.ncat_muscle and the rest of XrayAttenuation's NCAT/XCAT catalog; or constructed inline, XA.Material(name, ZA_ratio, I, density, composition), for your own contrast bolus, calibration solution or alloy.

A Prebuilt NCAT Material

A Custom Contrast Material

A 5 mg/mL iodinated blood mixture, like a coronary CT-angiography bolus: start from ncat_blood's composition and add elemental iodine. Adding iodine_mg_per_mL mg of iodine per mL of blood at density ρ gives an iodine mass fraction of iodine_mg_per_mL / (1000 ρ) (ρ in g/cm³); the other elements are rescaled so the composition still sums to 1.

function build_iodine_blood(iodine_mg_per_mL::Real)
    base = BS.XA.Materials.ncat_blood
    density = base.density # ~1.06 g/cm³
    ρ_g_cm3 = ustrip(uconvert(u"g/cm^3", density))
    f_I = iodine_mg_per_mL / (1000.0 * ρ_g_cm3) # iodine mass fraction
    scale = 1.0 - f_I

    comp = Dict{Int, Float64}()
    for (Z, frac) in base.composition
        comp[Z] = frac * scale
    end
    comp[53] = get(comp, 53, 0.0) + f_I # add iodine

    return BS.XA.Material(
        "Iodine-blood ($(iodine_mg_per_mL) mg/mL)",
        # ZA shifts ~negligibly at clinical dose
        base.ZA_ratio,
        # likewise for excitation energy
        base.I,
        density,
        comp,
    )
end;
iodine_blood = build_iodine_blood(5.0);

What the iodine does: below its K-edge at 33.2 keV iodine absorbs like any heavy element, and just above it absorbs far more, right where a 120 kVp spectrum is rich in photons. Five milligrams per millilitre is a mass fraction under half a percent, yet it lifts the blood's attenuation visibly at every energy of the spectrum.

The Name → Material Map

The loader ships the canonical NCAT/XCAT mapping as BS.xcat_default_materials(): every XCIST material name → an XrayAttenuation material. This is what replaces hand-parsing a per-organ spreadsheet: the compositions already live in XrayAttenuation's NCAT catalog. Copy the dict, edit it by name, and hand it back to the loader with materials =.

Override a Material

Copy the default map and reassign by XCIST name: here the blood pool becomes the 5 mg/mL iodine_blood built above, so the heart chambers and great vessels light up like a contrast-enhanced CTA. The edited map goes to the loader in section 3.

materials_map = let m = BS.xcat_default_materials()
    m["ncat_blood"] = iodine_blood # dope the blood pool with 5 mg/mL iodine contrast
    m
end;

3. Build the Phantom

load_xcat_male_slab returns the labeled pieces; we assemble the Phantom from them. For a GPU simulation the mask must live on the device (the workspace picks its compute backend from the mask's array type), so we to_gpu it first. The slab is a single axial section at the phantom's full in-plane resolution: real anatomy at a docs-friendly compute cost, with no downsampling.

xcat = try
    # full-resolution single slab
    BS.load_xcat_male_slab(; materials = materials_map, quiet = true)
catch err
    @warn "XCAT download/load failed; the compute cells will skip" exception = err
    nothing
end;
phantom_labeled = xcat === nothing ? nothing : xcat.mask;
VOXEL_SIZE_CM = xcat === nothing ? (0.15, 0.15, 0.15) : xcat.voxel_size_cm;
phantom = xcat === nothing ?
    nothing :
    BS.Phantom(to_gpu(xcat.mask), xcat.materials, xcat.voxel_size_cm);

4. Scan

The GE Revolution Apex Elite of notebook 01, REVOLUTION_APEX. The protocol is a body CTA: 120 kVp / 250 mA, 5 mm collimation, 500 views in 1 s, each view integrated over the arc the gantry turns through while the detector reads it (view_samples = 5). Reconstruction: 512 × 512 over 35 cm, eight 0.625 mm slices.

# `projector` picks the forward ray tracer: :dd_fast (default) is distance-driven and
# anti-aliased, and walks the volume once for the whole spectrum; :siddon point-samples
# the volume and can alias in strongly beam-hardened regions. The Hybrid-IR cell reads
# `sim_opts.projector`, so its system matrix always matches the operator that made the data.
# `view_samples = 5`: the detector integrates each view while the gantry turns (notebook 01).
sim_opts = BS.SimOptions(seed = 1234, projector = :dd_fast, view_samples = 5);
recon_opts = BS.ReconOptions(matrix_size = (512, 512, 8), fov_cm = 35.0, z_cm = 0.5);

The notebook 01 pattern: create_workspace, simulate!, copy the sinogram off the device, release the device buffers. simulate! returns the acquisition's dose report.

sim = phantom === nothing ?
    nothing :
    let
        @info "Simulating XCAT body CTA: 120 kVp / 250 mA…"
        ws = BS.create_workspace(scanner, protocol, sim_opts, recon_opts, phantom)
        out = BS.simulate!(ws, phantom, protocol, sim_opts)

        result = (sino = Array(ws.sinogram), geom = ws.geom, dose = out.dose)

        ws = nothing
        GC.gc(true)

        result
    end;
DoseReport (body32, 120 kVp, 250.0 mAs/rotation, axial, increment 5.0 mm) CTDIvol = 17.15 mGy DLP = 8.58 mGy·cm over 0.5 cm CTDIw = 6.861 mGy/100 mAs (centre 4.151, periphery 8.217; ±0.48 % statistical) free-in-air kerma at isocentre = 16.16 mGy/100 mAs N·T = 5.0 mm, beam 5.0 mm, filters [("aluminum", 2.5), ("Al", 4.5)], bowtie :ge_revolution_large
sim === nothing ? md"" : sim.dose

5. Reconstruct

The chain of notebook 01, applied with both algorithms: the water beam-hardening correction, calibrated per detector column from the full detected spectrum (no tunable parameters), then FBP or Hybrid IR, then HU with the correction's own water μ.

Noise is already in the counts

Quantum noise and the electronic noise of scanner.electronic_noise are both added by simulate! to the detector counts, before the log, where a real detector adds them. The reconstruction sees all of it, so iterative reconstruction can reduce all of it. Adding noise to the HU volume after reconstruction would be identical for FBP and HIR by construction.

The Water BHC

One calibration for the 120 kVp beam (2.5 mm flat filter + 4.5 mm Al + bowtie). It returns a WaterBHC with one polynomial per detector column and its reference μ_water_ref, used by both reconstructions.

bhc_calibration = sim === nothing ?
    nothing :
    let
        # Parameter-free water BHC — physics only, no tunables, no thresholds:
        # per-column poly→mono polynomials from the FULL detected spectrum
        # (tube × filters × bowtie × heel × η(E) — whatever sim_opts enabled).
        model = BS.calibrate_bhc_water(
            sim_opts,
            protocol;
            scanner = scanner,
            geom = sim.geom,
        )

        (model = model, μ_water = model.μ_water_ref, ref_E_keV = model.reference_energy_keV)
    end;

Calibrated: reference energy 74.7 keV, water μ 0.18816 cm⁻¹.

FBP

Water BHC → FDK with the :standard kernel → HU, releasing the device buffers at the end.

hu_fbp = sim === nothing ?
    nothing :
    let
        sino_gpu = BS.apply_bhc_water(to_gpu(sim.sino), bhc_calibration.model)
        ws_fdk = BS.create_fdk_recon_workspace(sino_gpu, sim.geom, recon_opts.matrix_size)
        recon_μ = BS.reconstruct!(ws_fdk, sino_gpu, sim.geom)
        hu = Float32.(BS.to_hounsfield(Array(recon_μ); μ_water = bhc_calibration.μ_water))
        ws_fdk = nothing
        sino_gpu = nothing
        recon_μ = nothing
        GC.gc(true)
        hu
    end;

Hybrid IR

The same chain with create_hir_recon_workspace(...; strength = 60) in place of the FDK workspace: an FBP start, then ordered-subsets penalised weighted least squares with an edge-preserving Huber prior, the open-literature (Fessler) counterpart of the vendor hybrid IR algorithms (GE ASIR-V, Siemens SAFIRE, Philips iDose⁴, Canon AIDR 3D), whose noise-reduction range its strength table targets.

One dial: strength

A percentage in steps of 10, read like the GE ASIR-V dial: 0 is pure FBP (the iterative loop is skipped), 60 the standard clinical setting used here, 100 the maximum noise reduction. It moves the regularisation weight, the Huber threshold, the relaxation and the number of epochs together along one calibrated trajectory.

Projector consistency

Hybrid IR's data term uses a forward projector, which must be the one that generated the sinogram. The cell passes projector = sim_opts.projector, so changing the simulation's projector keeps the reconstruction consistent. FBP has no forward projector and is unaffected.

hu_hir = sim === nothing ?
    nothing :
    let
        sino_gpu = BS.apply_bhc_water(to_gpu(sim.sino), bhc_calibration.model)
        ws_hir = BS.create_hir_recon_workspace(
            sino_gpu,
            sim.geom,
            recon_opts.matrix_size;
            strength = 60,
            projector = sim_opts.projector,
        )
        recon_μ = BS.reconstruct!(ws_hir, sino_gpu, sim.geom)
        hu = Float32.(BS.to_hounsfield(Array(recon_μ); μ_water = bhc_calibration.μ_water))
        ws_hir = nothing
        sino_gpu = nothing
        recon_μ = nothing
        GC.gc(true)
        hu
    end;

6. FBP vs Hybrid IR

Where the Noise Is Measured

A box near the image centre spans lung to iodinated blood, so its standard deviation is anatomy, not noise, and would hide what HIR does. The phantom labels are carried onto the reconstruction grid with BS.resample_to_recon and the myocardium label is eroded by 2 pixels, so only pixels surrounded by myocardium are measured.

# The myocardium, eroded: a pixel counts only if every in-plane neighbour within r is myocardium
# too (boundary pixels mix two tissues, and their spread is the edge, not the noise)
myocardium = hu_fbp === nothing || hu_hir === nothing ?
    nothing :
    let
        labels = BS.resample_to_recon(phantom, sim.geom, recon_opts.matrix_size)
        heart = first(k for (k, v) in xcat.label_names if v == "ncat_heart")
        r = 2
        nx, ny, nz = size(labels)
        roi = [
            CartesianIndex(i, j, k)
            for k in 1:nz, j in (1 + r):(ny - r), i in (1 + r):(nx - r)
            if all(labels[i + di, j + dj, k] == heart for dj in -r:r, di in -r:r)
        ]
        (
            labels = labels,
            roi = roi,
            fbp = (mean = Float64(mean(hu_fbp[roi])), σ = Float64(std(hu_fbp[roi]))),
            hir = (mean = Float64(mean(hu_hir[roi])), σ = Float64(std(hu_hir[roi]))),
        )
    end;

The Images

Both reconstructions share the whole chain except the algorithm. The soft-tissue window (W 850 / L 125) shows the iodine-enhanced blood pools of the cardiac chambers and the difference in noise texture between the two.

Noise inside the myocardium (12336 pixels, all slices)

AlgorithmMean (HU)σ (HU)
FBP47.316.4
Hybrid IR, strength 6047.311.7

Hybrid IR lowers the noise by 28.6 % and leaves the mean where it was. The package's calibration band for strength 60 is 25–35 %.

Summary

Three ideas on top of the five-struct API of notebook 01:

  • Voxel phantoms from an artifact. BS.load_xcat_male_slab() (and the other load_xcat_* loaders) download a published XCAT phantom once, verify it, and return the labeled mask, a material per label and the voxel size; BS.Phantom(to_gpu(mask), materials, voxel_size) makes it simulatable. Any other labeled mask works the same way.

  • Materials you define. XA.Materials.ncat_* for the standard tissues, or XA.Material(name, ZA, I, density, composition) for a contrast bolus, a calibration solution or an alloy; the composition is a Dict of atomic number → mass fraction, and the loader's materials = keyword swaps it in by XCIST name. Here 5 mg/mL of iodine is a mass fraction of 0.47 %.

  • Hybrid IR. create_hir_recon_workspace(sino, geom, matrix; strength) in place of the FDK workspace: the same reconstruct! call, lower noise at the same mean HU.

On this scan (CTDIvol 17.15 mGy), Hybrid IR at strength 60 lowered the myocardium noise from 16.4 to 11.7 HU (28.6 %) with the mean moving by 0.1 HU.
